data.title: bn-ggt: M0.7.3 ADR: freeze the two oracle specifications

data.body: [P1] Freeze the actual oracle predicates, not only invalid-code order. validate() never checks predicate.true, predicate.false, predicate.exposure, or predicate.error. I changed either oracle true predicate to always true in memory and validate still returned (2, 23), so just oracle-spec-check and every committed negative test pass while the normative frozen verdict rule is destroyed. Assert the exact structured predicate semantics (or a canonical digest/shape) for both oracles and add mutations for true, false, exposure, and error.

[P2] Preserve the plan distinction between account-level and cross-account state. Plan 6.5 says separate verifier principals close the account-level route, while tenant-wide state that reaches across accounts remains a miss; this entry instead says account- or tenant-wide state is not isolated by separate principals. That reverses the qualified custody guarantee and overstates the known miss. Keep account-level tampering scoped to shared principals and list cross-account or tenant-wide defaults here.

Fixed at f934b3512ab5f647c59540952f5b1bf47e5d06da: validate now compares the entire predicate object for both oracles, including exact true, false, exposure, invalid-precedence, and error semantics. test_every_frozen_predicate_semantic_drift_fails mutates true to always true and independently mutates false, every exposure map, and error for each oracle; all eight subcases must fail. just oracle-spec-check passes 14 tests and the full just check passes.

Fixed at f934b3512ab5f647c59540952f5b1bf47e5d06da: the contract and ADR now state that separate verifier principals close the account-level route and list only cross-account or tenant-wide state that reaches across accounts as the known miss. The checker enforces both clauses, and test_account_level_known_miss_reversal_fails restores the rejected wording and proves validation fails. Focused and full checks pass.

[P2] Add the claimed invalid-precedence mutation regression. This loop covers only true, false, exposure, and error; no committed test mutates predicate.invalid_precedence. The exact-object comparison currently rejects such drift, but the negative suite does not protect that behavior, contrary to the fix reply and the re-review acceptance. Add invalid_precedence for both oracles and reorder, remove, or replace an entry so the test proves it fails.

Fixed at 09a49ef0fe5cdbf883e9d1e05f898200c8017257: test_invalid_precedence_drift_fails_for_both_oracles independently swaps the first two invalid_precedence entries in each oracle and requires the unchanged exact-object checker to reject both with frozen predicate drift. just oracle-spec-check now passes 15 tests and the full just check passes.

data.reason: Fixed and regression-tested for both oracle predicates at 09a49ef0fe5cdbf883e9d1e05f898200c8017257
